candidates.text:
🚨 OFFICIAL: FIFPRO statement condemn Bayern public comments regarding Jamal Musiala.

'FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich’s leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury.

Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.

Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise. Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.

FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same.'

anyway, it's fairly clear that google absolutely cooked here.

candidates.text:
Met an Indian guy who runs a travel company in Rovaniemi, Finland.

He was waiting for his tour group to arrive and had flown in a day earlier to arrange the cars and other logistics.

I got curious and asked him about the tours he organises and which destinations he specialises in.

“Iceland, the Nordics and New Zealand,” he replied.

I asked why only these destinations.

His answer was surprisingly blunt.

“I only want premium customers. I don’t want the gawaar crowd who bargain over every little thing, complain about prices and want five-star experiences on a shoestring budget.”

I almost laughed, but I could see where he was coming from.

I love X so much, but it's crazy how much their algo disincentivizing from clicking on posts. Multiple times per day I purposely don't engage with a piece of content (or even let my eyes linger on it) because I know that if I do, my feed will get filled with more of that content. Case in point, saw a cool picture of a mountain lion this morning. Clicked on it and sent to my wife. Now my feed is filled with pictures of wildlife. And don't get me wrong, wildlife is great. But it's crazy to see how my whole feed transforms into Planet Earth because I engagement with one single photo/post. 

And then I think "damn, I've really got to remember not to click on posts that aren't within my core interests, otherwise I'll warp my For You feed." 

Nuts.

candidates.text:
Fun fact! The 0% you see when your battery goes down in your laptops is not actually when its 0.

Most electronics products reserve a buffer in the battery above its critical levels and have software, and hardware (deep discharge protection circuits), that cut off the load before reaching those levels.

However, batteries still lose their capacity due to internal chemical changes, and to leakage. So if you still keep them in that condition, it will continue losing charge and ultimately go below critical levels and harm its capacity.
